hook: A set of 1970s office equipment that is, biologically speaking, alive, and that claims to be a former Foundation administrator. The tone is dry and quietly funny. Read the procedures closely, because each odd feeding instruction makes sense once the description explains it.
whyItMatters: SCP-086 is a good example of the wiki's bureaucratic humor: an anomaly that behaves more like a model employee than a threat. Its object class line, which flips back and forth, sums up the joke before the article even begins. It carries the rewrite tag, so the current text is a reworked version.
thingsToNotice:
The neat trick here is that the entity raises doubts about itself. It points out that there is no way to prove it really is the man it remembers, which is a more unsettling idea than anything in the anatomy section. The acquisition log then shows it insisting on its own containment.

The closing notes turn that sincerity into comedy: the object lobbies to be taken more seriously and is politely turned down. Small physical details, like the ringing it finds unpleasant, also help make a desk full of supplies feel like a person.

related.note: Another mind living inside dated hardware, with a much grumpier temperament.
A gentle, talkative entity you mostly get to know through what it asks for.
